interpretation: Conditional pinned-source attribution. A resolved predicate resolves only its stated source boundary, not binary equivalence or physical resource effects.

callback_assignment.claim: WLAN supplies a stack callback object; common registration copies its function pointers, and common Wi-Fi-on invokes the registered WLAN probe. Direction is common-to-WLAN.
callback_assignment.boundary: Exact definitions/assignments in the selected AHB/WMT source branch. The stack object itself is not retained; copied callbacks are globals. HifAhbPltmProbe ignores registration's return and returns zero.
callback_assignment.missing: No missing assignment edge; actual built-in initialization and active binary equivalence remain outside this resolved source boundary.
callback_assignment.next_discriminator: Close the common compile guard and exported built-in initialization caller before claiming this is an executed selected-image chain.

function_on_to_firmware.claim: The conditional source chain joins WIFI_write to queued WMT operation dispatch, common Wi-Fi callback, HifAhbProbe, wlanProbe and the local firmware buffer passed to wlanAdapterStart.
function_on_to_firmware.boundary: The caller maps then synchronously calls AdapterStart then unmaps the buffer on return, including AdapterStart failure. Mapping failure skips the caller unmap; mapping's load-failure path frees/closes. The request_firmware alternative is disabled. Queue waiting and worker execution are separate contexts; timeout is not completion proof.
function_on_to_firmware.missing: CFG_FUNC_WIFI_SUPPORT definition/common build closure and the exact built-in init caller were not selected before the three-batch cap. No OSAL timeout/cancellation or callback synchronization guarantee is established.
function_on_to_firmware.next_discriminator: A fresh narrow build/include and built-in init selection audit, plus separately scoped queue timeout/callback synchronization proof; no device test is admitted.

common_lifetime.claim: A universal rule that common power is held before, throughout and after every WLAN probe callback is contradicted by the deferred-registration source path.
common_lifetime.boundary: Normal queued success establishes WMT FUNC_ON before callback and promotes Wi-Fi state only after zero return, with no common release in that synchronous path. But a missing callback sets gWifiProbed and returns -2; core failure may power down when all consumers are off. System-state-reset does not clear that pending flag. Registration later directly invokes it, without reacquiring common power or promoting the normal Wi-Fi state in that body. This is a source path, not a claim it happened.
common_lifetime.missing: No universal reference lifetime is proved. Concurrent resets/unregister, timeout and physical rail/clock retention are unjoined. WMT_STAT_PWR is changed before the platform effect returns, so it cannot certify effect success.
common_lifetime.next_discriminator: Separate normal and late-registration protocols; prove exclusion or recovery of late registration and synchronization before proposing a retained provider reference.

failure_propagation.claim: The inspected branches distinguish callback error, missing callback, common driver status and pending registration state; failures are not success-state promotions.
failure_propagation.boundary: wlanProbe failure causes pfWlanRemove and -1 at HIF; common maps nonzero callback to -1 and missing callback to -2, setting its Wi-Fi bit only on zero. Core sets Wi-Fi POWER_OFF on callback failure and conditionally requests common power-off if all listed consumers are off; other active consumers keep common state. It preserves the function-on error even if cleanup fails. POWER_OFF bookkeeping may be set despite a failed power-off effect; a disabled power-off flag refuses that operation. Late-registration callback failure returns -2 without clearing the pending flag or copied callbacks. Host-awake get/put is per request, not a retained WLAN-provider reference.
failure_propagation.missing: Resolved at the inspected source return/state boundary only. Timeout execution completion, deeper effect status, cleanup correctness and concurrent state coherence are not established.
failure_propagation.next_discriminator: Independently audit OSAL timeout ownership and all state writers before runtime/refcount conclusions; do not infer resource release from POWER_OFF bookkeeping.

cleanup_order.claim: Function-off, probe failure and unregister have distinct visible cleanup orders, not one proved symmetric provider-release contract.
cleanup_order.boundary: Function-off calls WLAN remove before clearing Wi-Fi bit on callback success; core marks Wi-Fi POWER_OFF even on callback failure, then may power off all-common state and overwrite the earlier return with power-off result. HIF remove calls wlanRemove then PALDO-off request and returns zero. Probe failure calls pfWlanRemove directly, not HifAhbRemove, after wlanProbe's own failure switch. Unregister calls wlanRemove then platform_driver_unregister; the platform remove body only clears callbacks and does not request function-off. The selected makefile defines built-in mode, while the driver remove field uses __exit_p; a module-unload guarantee cannot be assumed.
cleanup_order.missing: Exact __exit_p/build selection and invocation of built-in exit are unjoined. No proof that probe-failure's additional remove is safe, that its PALDO request is balanced, or that unregister synchronizes an in-flight callback. This audit does not repair these paths.
cleanup_order.next_discriminator: A separate narrow built-in exit/__exit_p and failure-cleanup lifetime review with complete resource acquisition/release tables, before any Linux ownership or reuse proposal.

state_model.normal_during: no common release in synchronous call chain
state_model.host_awake_reference: released after queue wait returns, including timeout

escalation.evidence: Deferred registration bypasses normal common on/state promotion; bookkeeping and effect status differ; cleanup paths are asymmetric.
escalation.attempts: Three frozen public-fetch batches; 26 successful requests; four newly selected regular files; no repair or device attempt. Two declared contextual rereads, plus incidental repeated locator context. Unmeasured initial freeze labels removed rather than represented as clock evidence.
escalation.unresolved_question: Can any selected-image, synchronized common-provider lifetime be certified across late registration, request timeout and built-in unregister? Not from this bounded corpus.
escalation.next_discriminating_check: New separately scoped common build/include + built-in initialization/exit audit; then exact callback/OSAL synchronization and resource balancing review. No further reads under this item.
